name: sidesim
description: A live, interactive iOS Simulator embedded in VS Code — video mirror with tap, drag, keyboard, and two-finger pinch input.

enumDescriptions: Prefer the native simhelper sidecar, then idb_companion, then the idb CLI.
Always use the native simhelper sidecar (correct H.264 video, in-process HID). Fails if the binary is missing.
Always use the idb_companion gRPC backend (low-latency input and video). Fails if idb_companion is not installed.
Always use the idb command-line backend.
sidesim.simulator.backend.description: How the simulator panel connects to booted simulators for video and input.

sidesim.simulator.sandbox.description: Run the simhelper sidecar under sandbox-exec (no network access, file writes limited to CoreSimulator and temp directories).

sidesim.simulator.fps.description: Video frame rate. Applied when a panel opens (the stream is fixed for the panel's lifetime).

sidesim.simulator.scale.description: Video resolution as a fraction of the simulator's native resolution. Applied when a panel opens.

sidesim.run.command.markdownDescription:
Shell command run by the panel's **▶ Run** button to build, install, and launch your app on the booted simulator. Build-system-agnostic — you supply the command. The target device's UDID is exported as `$SIDESIM_TARGET_UDID`, and it runs in the workspace root.

Examples:
- Bazel (rules_apple): `bazel run //path/to:MyApp`
- Bazel + explicit target: `bazel build //app:MyApp && xcrun simctl install "$SIDESIM_TARGET_UDID" bazel-bin/app/MyApp.app && xcrun simctl launch "$SIDESIM_TARGET_UDID" com.example.MyApp`
- Xcode: `xcodebuild -scheme MyApp -destination "id=$SIDESIM_TARGET_UDID" && xcrun simctl launch "$SIDESIM_TARGET_UDID" com.example.MyApp`

scripts.vscode:prepublish: npm run build:sidecar && npm run check-types && npm run bundle
scripts.pretest: npm run compile && npm run lint
